A

Chapter Overview

Welcome to Chapter 2. In this chapter, you will learn how to tell past experiences in English using recount text.

Pada bab ini, kalian akan belajar menceritakan pengalaman masa lalu menggunakan Bahasa Inggris. Pengalaman itu bisa berupa pengalaman liburan, mengikuti festival budaya digital, mengikuti webinar, mengikuti lomba sekolah, membantu kegiatan masyarakat, mengikuti kegiatan literasi, atau mengikuti kegiatan edukatif di wilayah kepulauan.

Sometimes, a simple experience can teach us something important. Maybe you once joined a school competition. Maybe you helped prepare a cultural festival. Maybe you attended an online webinar when the internet connection was unstable. Maybe you visited another island by boat and learned something new. Maybe you joined a beach-cleaning activity and wrote about it in your journal.

Through recount text, you can share what happened, when it happened, who was involved, what you did, and what lesson you learned.

Big Question: How can we retell our past experiences clearly, meaningfully, and confidently in English?

B

Learning Objectives

After learning this chapter, you are expected to be able to:

  • identify the social function of recount text;
  • analyze the structure of recount text: orientation, events, and reorientation;
  • identify past events in oral and written texts;
  • use simple past tense to retell past experiences;
  • use regular and irregular action verbs correctly;
  • use time connectors such as then, after that, before, next, finally, and later;
  • read and understand recount texts about school activities, digital events, competitions, and holidays;
  • write a personal recount text in the form of an e-journal;
  • create a vlog draft about a past educational or holiday experience;
  • reflect on the lesson learned from a past experience.
C

Mindful Starter: Remember, Feel, Share

Sebelum belajar, pikirkan satu pengalaman yang pernah kamu alami. Pengalaman sederhana juga bisa menjadi cerita bermakna.

Situation 1

Joining a Digital Cultural Festival

Last month, students from an island school joined a digital cultural festival. They recorded a short video about traditional food, local songs, and coastal life. The internet connection was weak, but they worked together and uploaded the video successfully.

Bulan lalu, siswa dari sekolah kepulauan mengikuti festival budaya digital. Mereka merekam video singkat tentang makanan tradisional, lagu daerah, dan kehidupan pesisir.

Situation 2

Attending an Online Webinar

A student attended a webinar about digital literacy. At first, the signal was unstable. The student missed some parts of the presentation. After that, the student asked a friend for notes and wrote a summary in English.

Seorang siswa mengikuti webinar literasi digital. Sinyal sempat tidak stabil, lalu ia meminta catatan teman.

Situation 3

Joining a School Competition

A group of students joined an English storytelling competition. They practiced after school, prepared their script, and performed confidently. They did not win first place, but they learned teamwork and courage.

Siswa mengikuti lomba storytelling Bahasa Inggris dan belajar kerja sama serta keberanian.

Reflection Questions

D

What Is Recount Text?

Recount text is a text that retells past events or experiences in chronological order.

Recount text adalah teks yang menceritakan kembali peristiwa atau pengalaman masa lalu secara berurutan. The word recount means to tell again.

Social Function

The social function of recount text is to retell past events or experiences and share what happened. Sometimes, recount text also shares feelings, lessons, or reflections from the experience.

Examples of Recount Text Topics

TopicExample
Holiday experienceMy Trip to a Nearby Island
School competitionMy First English Storytelling Competition
Webinar experienceJoining a Digital Literacy Webinar
Digital cultural festivalOur Digital Cultural Festival Project
Educational visitVisiting a Local Seaweed Farm
Community activityJoining a Beach-Cleaning Program
Personal learning experienceMy First Time Creating an E-Journal
School projectPreparing a Vlog Draft for English Class

Recount Text vs Descriptive Text

AspectDescriptive TextRecount Text
PurposeTo describe a person/place/objectTo retell past events
Main tenseSimple present tenseSimple past tense
StructureIdentification + descriptionOrientation + events + reorientation
Example topicAn inspiring figureMy experience joining a webinar
Time focusGeneral factsPast time
Common wordsis, has, creates, inspireswent, joined, watched, learned

Structure of Recount Text

1. Orientation

Introduces who, when, where, and what happened.

Example: Last Friday, my classmates and I joined an online webinar about digital literacy at school.

2. Events

Tells what happened in chronological order using connectors such as first, then, after that, before, finally.

Example: First, we entered the Zoom meeting. Then, the speaker explained how to check information online.

3. Reorientation

Closes the story with final feeling, lesson learned, personal reflection, or closing comment.

Example: It was a useful experience. I learned that we must check facts before sharing information online.

Simple Recount Text Structure

PartFunctionExample
TitleGives the topicMy First Digital Cultural Festival
OrientationIntroduces who, when, where, whatLast month, our class joined a digital cultural festival.
Event 1Tells the first eventFirst, we discussed the theme.
Event 2Tells the next eventThen, we recorded a video about local culture.
Event 3Tells another eventAfter that, we edited the video together.
ReorientationGives feeling/lessonI felt proud because we could introduce our island culture.
F

Grammar Lab: Simple Past Tense, Action Verbs, and Time Connectors

Recount text uses the past because it tells what happened before now.

1. Function of Simple Past Tense

Simple past tense is used to talk about actions or situations that happened in the past. Simple past tense digunakan untuk membicarakan tindakan atau keadaan yang terjadi di masa lalu.

Common Past Time Expressions

Time ExpressionArti Bahasa IndonesiaExample
yesterdaykemarinI joined a webinar yesterday.
last nighttadi malamI wrote my journal last night.
last weekminggu laluWe practiced last week.
last monthbulan laluThey joined a festival last month.
last yeartahun laluShe visited Makassar last year.
two days agodua hari laluHe uploaded the video two days ago.
three weeks agotiga minggu laluWe started the project three weeks ago.
in 2025pada tahun 2025I joined a competition in 2025.
on Mondaypada hari SeninWe presented our vlog draft on Monday.
during the holidayselama liburanI visited my grandmother during the holiday.

Simple Past Sentence Patterns

PatternFormulaExamples
Positive SentenceSubject + Verb 2 + Object/ComplementI joined a webinar yesterday. / We visited a nearby island last week. / She wrote an e-journal last night.
Negative SentenceSubject + did not/didn’t + Verb 1 + Object/ComplementI did not join the competition. / We didn’t upload the video on time.
Yes/No QuestionDid + Subject + Verb 1 + Object/Complement?Did you join the webinar? Yes, I did. / Did she write an e-journal? No, she didn’t.
Wh-QuestionQuestion Word + did + Subject + Verb 1 + Object/Complement?What did you do yesterday? / Where did you go last week? / How did you feel after the competition?
Important Note: After did not/didn’t, use Verb 1, not Verb 2. Correct: She didn’t write the journal. Incorrect: She didn’t wrote the journal.

Time Connectors

Time connectors help readers understand the order of events. Time connectors membantu pembaca memahami urutan kejadian.

Time ConnectorArti Bahasa IndonesiaFunctionExample
firstpertama-tamastarts the first eventFirst, we prepared the script.
beforesebelumshows an earlier actionBefore the webinar, I checked the internet connection.
thenkemudianshows the next eventThen, we joined the meeting.
after thatsetelah itushows another next eventAfter that, we answered a quiz.
nextberikutnyacontinues the sequenceNext, we discussed the topic.
laterkemudian/nantishows a later eventLater, we wrote a reflection.
suddenlytiba-tibashows unexpected eventSuddenly, the signal disappeared.
finallyakhirnyashows the last eventFinally, we submitted the vlog draft.
at the endpada akhirnyacloses the sequenceAt the end, we felt proud.
duringselamashows something happening within a periodDuring the festival, we learned many things.
whileketika/sementarashows two actions happening togetherWhile my friend edited the video, I wrote the caption.

Building a Sequence

Less Clear

We recorded a video. We discussed the theme. We uploaded the project. We edited the sound.

Better

First, we discussed the theme. Then, we recorded a video. After that, we edited the sound. Finally, we uploaded the project.

Versi kedua lebih jelas karena menggunakan time connectors.

Model Texts

Baca contoh teks berikut. Perhatikan orientation, events, reorientation, simple past tense, action verbs, dan time connectors.

Model Text 1: Our First Digital Cultural Festival

Orientation

Last month, my classmates and I joined a digital cultural festival at school. The festival was about local culture and creativity. Our English teacher asked us to make a short video about island life, traditional food, and positive values in our community.

Events

First, we discussed the theme in our group. We chose “Life by the Sea” because we wanted to show our daily life as students from a coastal area. Then, we wrote a simple script in English. We used easy sentences because we wanted the audience to understand our message clearly.

After that, we recorded several scenes near the beach, at school, and at a small traditional food stall. Some students explained local food, while others showed the beauty of the sea and the importance of keeping the beach clean. Before we recorded the final video, we practiced our pronunciation many times.

The most difficult part was the internet connection. The signal was weak when we tried to upload the video. We waited until night because the connection was better. Finally, we uploaded the video successfully.

Reorientation

It was a memorable experience. I felt proud because our group worked together and introduced our local culture in English. I learned that technology can help students from islands share their stories with more people.

PartInformation
OrientationLast month, the students joined a digital cultural festival at school.
Event 1They discussed the theme and chose “Life by the Sea.”
Event 2They wrote a simple script in English.
Event 3They recorded scenes near the beach, at school, and at a food stall.
Event 4They practiced pronunciation.
ProblemThe internet connection was weak.
Final eventThey uploaded the video successfully.
ReorientationThe writer felt proud and learned that technology can help island students share stories.

Model Text 2: My Experience Joining a Digital Literacy Webinar

Orientation

Two weeks ago, I joined an online webinar about digital literacy. The webinar was organized for high school students. I joined it from our classroom with my friends and our English teacher.

Events

Before the webinar started, we prepared our notebooks and checked the internet connection. At first, everything went well. The speaker introduced the topic and explained why digital literacy was important for teenagers.

Then, the speaker talked about online safety. She taught us not to share passwords, home addresses, or private information online. She also explained how to check facts before sharing news on social media.

Suddenly, the signal became unstable. I missed some parts of the explanation. I felt worried because I wanted to understand the topic. After that, I asked my friend for notes. My friend helped me and explained the missing points.

At the end of the webinar, we answered a short quiz. I did not get a perfect score, but I understood the main message.

Reorientation

The webinar was very useful. I learned that being active online is not enough. We must also be careful, respectful, and responsible. After the webinar, I promised myself to check information before sharing it.

PartInformation
OrientationThe writer joined a digital literacy webinar two weeks ago.
Event 1The students prepared notebooks and checked the connection.
Event 2The speaker introduced digital literacy.
Event 3The speaker explained online safety and fact-checking.
ProblemThe signal became unstable.
SolutionThe writer asked a friend for notes.
Final eventThe students answered a quiz.
ReorientationThe writer learned to be careful, respectful, and responsible online.

Model Text 3: My First English Storytelling Competition

Orientation

Last semester, I joined an English storytelling competition at school. It was my first time speaking English in front of many students. I felt nervous, but I wanted to try my best.

Events

Before the competition, my group and I chose a local folktale. We wrote the script together and practiced after school. At first, I had difficulty pronouncing some words. My friends helped me repeat the words slowly.

Then, our teacher gave us feedback. She asked us to speak louder, use clear expression, and remember the sequence of the story. After that, we practiced again in the classroom. We also recorded our practice using a phone so we could watch and improve our performance.

On the competition day, I felt very nervous. My hands were cold, and I almost forgot the first sentence. However, my friend smiled at me and gave me confidence. Finally, we performed the story from beginning to end.

Reorientation

We did not win first place, but I felt proud. I learned that courage does not mean having no fear. Courage means trying your best even when you feel nervous.

PartInformation
OrientationThe writer joined an English storytelling competition last semester.
Event 1The group chose a local folktale.
Event 2They wrote the script and practiced after school.
Event 3The teacher gave feedback.
Event 4They recorded their practice.
ProblemThe writer felt nervous and almost forgot the first sentence.
Final eventThe group performed the story.
ReorientationThe writer learned the meaning of courage.

Model Text 4: A Short Trip to My Grandmother’s Island

Orientation

During the school holiday, I visited my grandmother on a nearby island. I went there with my father by boat. The trip took about two hours.

Events

Before we left home, my mother prepared rice, fried fish, and drinking water for the trip. We left the harbor early in the morning. The weather was sunny, and the sea was calm.

At first, I sat quietly because I felt sleepy. Then, I looked at the sea and saw several small fishing boats. My father told me the names of some islands that we passed. I took a few photos, but I did not post them immediately because the signal was weak.

After we arrived, my grandmother welcomed us warmly. She cooked simple food for lunch. In the afternoon, I helped my cousins collect dried seaweed near the shore. It was tiring, but I enjoyed it because I learned something about their daily life.

Reorientation

The trip was simple but meaningful. I learned that family, nature, and local work are important parts of island life. I also learned to appreciate the hard work of people who live near the sea.

Reading Comprehension

Read the text carefully.

My First Webinar Certificate

Last month, my school held a digital learning program for Grade X students. One of the activities was an online webinar about safe and positive social media use. I joined the webinar from the school library with five classmates.

Before the webinar began, we prepared our notebooks and connected the laptop to the projector. Our teacher reminded us to write important points. At 9 a.m., the speaker started the presentation. She explained that students should think before posting anything online.

Then, the speaker showed examples of good and bad online behavior. She said that sharing useful information, writing polite comments, and checking facts were examples of positive digital behavior. She also reminded us not to share personal data online.

After that, we joined a short quiz. Some questions were easy, but some were difficult. I answered carefully and discussed one question with my friend. Finally, I got a certificate because I completed the webinar and the quiz.

I felt happy and proud. The webinar taught me that social media is not only for entertainment. It can also be used for learning, sharing good messages, and building a positive identity.

Speaking Practice

Gunakan pertanyaan dan pola kalimat berikut untuk menceritakan pengalaman masa lalu.

Activity 1: Pair Talk — “What Happened?”

QuestionArti Bahasa Indonesia
What experience do you want to share?Pengalaman apa yang ingin kamu ceritakan?
When did it happen?Kapan itu terjadi?
Where did it happen?Di mana itu terjadi?
Who joined the activity?Siapa yang ikut kegiatan itu?
What did you do first?Apa yang kamu lakukan pertama?
What happened after that?Apa yang terjadi setelah itu?
How did you feel?Bagaimana perasaanmu?
What did you learn?Apa yang kamu pelajari?

Activity 2: Mini Dialogue

Alya: Rian, did you join the English competition last week?

Rian: Yes, I did. It was my first competition.

Alya: How did you feel before the competition?

Rian: I felt very nervous. My hands were cold.

Alya: What did you do before performing?

Rian: First, I practiced with my group. Then, our teacher gave us feedback. After that, we recorded our practice.

Alya: Did you win?

Rian: No, we didn’t win first place. But we felt proud.

Alya: Why?

Rian: Because we tried our best and learned to be more confident.

Alya: That is a great experience.

Alya bertanya apakah Rian mengikuti lomba Bahasa Inggris minggu lalu. Rian menjawab bahwa itu adalah lomba pertamanya. Ia merasa gugup, tetapi tetap berlatih dengan kelompoknya.

Writing Section: Writing a Recount Text

Pada bagian ini, kalian akan menulis recount text tentang pengalaman masa lalu.

Topics You Can Choose

  • joining a school competition;
  • attending a webinar;
  • joining a digital cultural festival;
  • visiting another island;
  • helping a community activity;
  • creating a vlog or digital project;
  • joining a beach-cleaning activity;
  • spending a holiday with family;
  • learning something new during a school program.

Step-by-Step Writing Guide

Step 1

Choose one experience.

Step 2

Answer the orientation questions: what, when, where, who, why.

Step 3

List the events in order using first, then, after that, next, finally.

Step 4

Add feelings: before, during, after the event.

Step 5

Add a lesson learned.

Step 6

Write your draft: title, orientation, events, reorientation.

Writing Template


Student Draft and Revised Version

Student Draft

Last month, I join webinar about social media. I prepare notebook and pen. Then teacher share link. I click the link and enter online room. The speaker explain about privacy. After that signal become weak. I ask my friend note. Finally I get certificate. I feel happy because I learn new thing.

Revised Version

Last month, I joined a webinar about social media. Before the webinar started, I prepared my notebook and pen. Then, the teacher shared the meeting link. I clicked the link and entered the online room. The speaker explained how to protect our privacy online. After that, the signal became weak, so I asked my friend for notes. Finally, I got a certificate. I felt happy because I learned something new and useful.

ProblemExplanation
“I join”Recount text uses past tense: “I joined.”
“I prepare”Use past tense: “I prepared.”
“teacher share”Use past tense and article: “the teacher shared.”
“I click”Use past tense: “I clicked.”
“speaker explain”Use past tense: “the speaker explained.”
“signal become”Use past form: “the signal became.”
“I ask my friend note”Better: “I asked my friend for notes.”
“I get certificate”Better: “I got a certificate.”
“I feel”Use past tense: “I felt.”
“I learn new thing”Better: “I learned something new.”

Why is the revised version better? It uses simple past tense correctly, uses time connectors, gives a clear sequence of events, improves word choice, has better sentence structure, and sounds more natural.

Digital E-Journal Corner

An e-journal is a digital journal or diary. It can be written in a document, note-taking app, blog, or learning platform. Dalam chapter ini, e-journal kalian berbentuk recount text tentang pengalaman masa lalu.

PartContent
DateWhen you wrote the journal
TitleTopic of your experience
OrientationWho, when, where, what
EventsWhat happened in order
ReflectionHow you felt and what you learned
MediaPhoto, drawing, icon, or screenshot if appropriate

E-Journal Example

Date: Monday, 8 June 2026

Title: My First Webinar Experience

Last Friday, I joined my first online webinar at school. The webinar was about safe social media use. I joined it from the classroom with my friends.

Before the webinar started, I prepared my notebook and pen. Then, my teacher shared the meeting link. After that, I entered the online room and listened to the speaker.

The speaker explained how to protect our privacy online. She also told us to check facts before sharing information. During the webinar, the signal became weak, but I asked my friend for notes.

Finally, I answered a quiz and got a certificate. I felt happy because I learned something useful. This experience taught me to be more responsible online.

Vlog Draft Corner

A vlog draft is a written plan or script before making a video blog. In this chapter, you do not have to make a full video. You can write a vlog draft first.

PartPurposeExample
OpeningGreets the audienceHi, everyone. Today, I want to share my experience.
OrientationGives backgroundLast week, I joined a school competition.
EventsTells what happenedFirst, we prepared the script. Then, we practiced.
FeelingShares emotionI felt nervous but excited.
LessonShares reflectionI learned to be more confident.
ClosingEnds the vlogThank you for listening. See you next time.

Vlog Draft Template


Vlog Speaking Tips

TipArti Bahasa Indonesia
Speak clearly.Berbicaralah dengan jelas.
Do not speak too fast.Jangan berbicara terlalu cepat.
Look at the camera.Lihat ke kamera.
Use simple sentences.Gunakan kalimat sederhana.
Practice before recording.Berlatih sebelum merekam.
Check your background.Periksa latar belakangmu.
Avoid sharing private information.Hindari membagikan informasi pribadi.
Be polite and positive.Bersikap sopan dan positif.

Common Mistakes in Recount Text

Mistake TypeIncorrectCorrectExplanation
Using present tenseI join a webinar yesterday.I joined a webinar yesterday.Gunakan past tense untuk yesterday.
Using Verb 2 after did notI didn’t joined the competition.I didn’t join the competition.Setelah didn’t gunakan Verb 1.
Wrong time orderWe uploaded the video. We wrote the script. We discussed the theme.First, we discussed the theme. Then, we wrote the script. Finally, we uploaded the video.Urutan peristiwa harus jelas.
Too few detailsI joined a webinar. It was good.Last Friday, I joined a webinar about digital literacy. The speaker explained online safety.Tambahkan detail waktu, tempat, dan pelajaran.
Forgetting feelings/reflectionWe joined a competition. We performed. We went home.I felt nervous but proud because we tried our best. I learned that practice builds confidence.Recount lebih bermakna dengan refleksi.

Project-Based Learning: Final Project

Project Title: My Digital Recount: E-Journal or Vlog Draft

Option 1: E-Journal

Write a digital journal entry about a past experience.

Option 2: Vlog Draft

Write a vlog script about a past holiday or educational experience.

Possible Topics

  • My first webinar experience
  • My school competition experience
  • My digital cultural festival experience
  • My holiday trip to another island
  • My experience helping a beach-cleaning activity
  • My experience creating a class video project
  • My experience joining an English club activity
  • My experience learning something new online
  • My experience helping my family during the holiday
  • My own meaningful past experience

Project Requirements

RequirementDescription
TitleClear and interesting
OrientationWho, when, where, what
EventsMinimum 4 events in order
Simple past tenseCorrect use of Verb 2
Action verbsMinimum 8 action verbs
Time connectorsMinimum 5 time connectors
FeelingsAt least 2 feelings
ReflectionLesson learned
Local contextConnect to school, island, coastal, digital, or community life
LanguageClear, polite, and understandable English

Project Timeline

MeetingActivity
Meeting 1Explore recount text and past experiences
Meeting 2Learn simple past tense, action verbs, and time connectors
Meeting 3Read model texts and analyze structure
Meeting 4Create Past Experience Map
Meeting 5Write e-journal or vlog draft
Meeting 6Peer feedback, revision, and presentation

Project Rubric

Criteria4 — Excellent3 — Good2 — Fair1 — Needs Improvement
ContentExperience is clear, meaningful, and detailed.Experience is clear with enough details.Experience is understandable but lacks details.Experience is unclear or incomplete.
StructureOrientation, events, and reorientation are complete and well-organized.Structure is complete with minor issues.Structure is partly complete.Structure is confusing or missing.
Simple Past TensePast tense is used accurately.Few past tense mistakes.Several past tense mistakes.Many mistakes that affect meaning.
Action VerbsUses many accurate action verbs.Uses enough action verbs.Uses limited action verbs.Uses very few action verbs.
Time ConnectorsUses time connectors naturally and clearly.Uses some time connectors correctly.Uses few time connectors.Time sequence is unclear.
VocabularyUses varied and relevant vocabulary.Uses appropriate vocabulary.Vocabulary is limited.Vocabulary is very limited or inaccurate.
ReflectionLesson learned is meaningful and personal.Lesson learned is clear.Reflection is simple.Reflection is missing or unclear.
Local/Digital ContextStrongly connects to school, island, coastal, or digital context.Shows some relevant context.Context is limited.No clear context.
PresentationClear, confident, and respectful.Mostly clear and respectful.Understandable but hesitant.Difficult to understand.

1LOTS

3LOTS

4LOTS

5LOTS

6LOTS

7LOTS

Bagian reorientation dalam recount text biasanya berisi….

8MOTS

11MOTS

12MOTS

Verb 2 dari kata “go” adalah….

13MOTS

14MOTS

15MOTS

16MOTS

A student writes: “Last week, I go to another island with my father.” The best revision is….

17HOTS

Read the paragraph. “Last Friday, we joined an English competition. First, we practiced our story. Then, our teacher gave us feedback. After that, we performed on stage. Finally, we received a certificate. I felt proud because I learned to be more confident.” Why is the paragraph a good recount paragraph?

18HOTS

A student wrote a recount text about joining a digital cultural festival. The events were clear, but the ending was missing. Which sentence is the best reorientation?

19HOTS

During a webinar, Sari learned that students should check facts before sharing news online. Two days later, she received a message about a sudden school holiday, but the message had no official source. What should Sari do based on her webinar experience?

20HOTS

A student wants to make a vlog draft about a holiday trip to a nearby island. Which opening is the most suitable?

21HOTS

A student writes: “Yesterday, our group prepare a vlog. First, we discuss the topic. Then, we record the introduction. After that, we upload the video.” Which revision is the best?

22HOTS

23HOTS

Read the recount text. “I joined a webinar. It was good. I learned something. It was nice.” What is the main weakness of the text?

Enrichment and Remedial Activities

Pilih kegiatan sesuai kebutuhan belajar.

Enrichment Activities

  • Create a One-Minute Vlog Script using at least 5 past tense verbs, 4 time connectors, 2 feelings, and 1 lesson learned.
  • Compare Two Experiences using topic, time, place, people involved, events, feelings, and lesson learned.
  • Make a Recount Comic Strip with 4 panels: orientation, first event, next event/problem, final event and lesson learned.
  • Write a Bilingual E-Journal in English with short Indonesian notes for difficult words.

Remedial Activities

  • Verb Card Practice: join–joined, go–went, write–wrote, make–made, upload–uploaded.
  • Simple Past Pattern Practice: Yesterday, I joined a webinar. Last week, we made a video. She wrote an e-journal last night. They submitted their project on time. He felt nervous before the competition.
  • Time Connector Practice: First, we discussed the topic. Then, we ________. After that, we ________. Finally, we ________.
  • Guided Recount Paragraph: Last ________, I ________. It happened in/at ________. First, I ________. Then, I ________. After that, I ________. Finally, I ________. I felt ________ because ________. I learned that ________.
AC

Assessment

Asesmen dilakukan secara diagnostik, formatif, sumatif, refleksi diri, dan peer feedback.

Diagnostic Assessment

  • What is one past experience you remember?
  • Can you mention three past tense verbs?
  • What is the difference between “join” and “joined”?
  • What time connectors do you know?
  • Have you ever written a journal or vlog script?

Formative Assessment

SkillActivity
ReadingReading comprehension
ListeningGap filling and sequencing
SpeakingPair talk and 60-second recount talk
GrammarSimple past tense practice
VocabularyAction verbs and feelings vocabulary
WritingRecount draft
Digital literacyE-journal/vlog draft planning

Summative Assessment

Final product: My Digital Recount: E-Journal or Vlog Draft. Students submit one e-journal entry or one vlog draft script.

Reading Comprehension Key
  • A digital learning program for Grade X students.
  • Safe and positive social media use.
  • In the school library.
  • They prepared notebooks and connected the laptop to the projector.
  • The teacher reminded them to write important points.
  • Students should think before posting anything online.
  • Sharing useful information, writing polite comments, and checking facts.
  • They joined a short quiz.
  • Because the writer completed the webinar and the quiz.
  • Happy and proud.
  • Social media can be used for learning, sharing good messages, and building a positive identity.
  • Examples: held, joined, prepared, connected, reminded, started, explained, showed, said, answered, got, felt, taught.
